To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the quality of lung cancer care in our network of health services was suboptimal in 2011 and 2) a quality improvement program based on a set of 11 indicators improved lung cancer care over the course of the project.

the use of clinical quality indicators (CQI) to improve the care of patients with lung cancer in a regional/rURAL network of health services (RNHS) was feasible and led to significant changes in the quality of care.

(a) the use of clinical indicators can help improve the quality of cancer care, (b) the use of indicators can also be an important tool in the process of quality improvement, (c) the use of a regional/rural health network can help improve the use of clinical guidelines and the quality of lung cancer care.

we have been able to demonstrate that a clinical quality indicator (CQI) can be used to improve lung cancer services in a regional/r rural network of health services, and that this has been achieved without the need for a major change in health services infrastructure.

we have been able to demonstrate that the implementation of a clinical quality improvement project can be successful in a rural/remote setting and that the use of clinical indicators can assist in the improvement process.
